Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:75: The Fifth Level – a Prohibition That Involves an Action: our Sages of blessed memory said, for a prohibition that involves an action, one is lashed, and the lashes are forty less one. And our Sages of blessed memory said: lashes stand in place of death. And they said: whoever is lashed and repeats the transgression is confined in a cell. And it is incumbent upon those who rebuke to search out the ways of the people, to investigate and know in what they stumble, and to warn them; for there are many warnings which, even though people keep part of the warning, they neglect in part — such as the prohibition of labor on the Sabbath, which most people keep, not profaning the Sabbath in the main, yet there are labors that some of the people are not careful about, because they are not known to them, and their error lodges with them, instead of their lodging among the wise, where they would seek Torah from their mouths. Therefore teachings have been transgressed and they have been punished, as it is said (Isaiah 26:10), "Let favor be shown to the wicked, yet he does not learn righteousness." And there are transgressors who stumble because they were not accustomed in their youth, in their father's house, to be careful of these things, and they inherited from their fathers and do not listen to the voice of their teachers — and these act presumptuously.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:76: And so all the people are careful about the blood of life and the blood that oozes out, yet some of them are not careful about the proper preparation of salting to remove the blood from the meat according to the law. And there are very many such things done unknowingly, with no one to rebuke, as it is said (Proverbs 29:18), "Where there is no vision, the people are unrestrained."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:77: And there are warnings that some of the multitude do not keep even in their essence, such as wounding and striking — for one who strikes his fellow transgresses two negative commandments, as it is said (Deuteronomy 25:3), "forty he may strike him, he shall not exceed... lest he add." And many transgress these prohibitions by striking their wives. And our Sages of blessed memory said: whoever raises his hand against his fellow, even though he did not strike him, is called wicked, as it is said (Exodus 2:13), "and he said to the wicked one, Why do you strike your fellow?" — it does not say "why did you strike," but "why do you strike." And Job said (Job 31:21), "if I have raised my hand against the orphan." And our Sages of blessed memory said: Rav Huna cut off the hand of one who struck [another], saying (Job 38:15), "and the raised arm shall be broken."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:78: And likewise concerning the destruction of the beard, as it is said (Leviticus 19:27), "and you shall not destroy the corner of your beard." And sinners leave the strand of hair [as a technicality] while the essential joints of the corners we do not know where they lie, so that they end up destroying the very corner of the beard; and rounding the corner of the head is forbidden even with scissors used in a manner like a razor.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:79: And there are people who are not careful concerning the forbidden mixture (kilayim) of shatnez, for they sew a woolen garment with linen thread, or make a linen border for the edge of a woolen garment.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:80: "None of you shall approach any that is near of kin to him" (Leviticus 18:6). Every bodily closeness is forbidden, such as touching the hand of a married woman; and its meaning is that this leads to the uncovering of nakedness, for closeness brings about forbidden relations. And should you say in your heart, Where do we find in Scripture that the Torah built a fence, that you should say it forbade the mere touch of hand to hand as a fence against transgression? — we shall answer you: behold, concerning the commandment of the nazirite, whose essential vow is lest he drink and forget the statute, or a spirit of licentiousness lead him astray, the Torah forbids him everything made from the grapevine, and all this as a fence to distance him from drinking wine. And so our Sages of blessed memory said in the Midrash.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:81: "And you shall not put a stumbling-block before the blind" (ibid. 19 [Leviticus 19:14]). Our Sages said that we have been warned by this not to strike one's grown son, lest it become a stumbling-block and cause him to sin with his tongue and to demean his father. And so we have been warned by this not to arrange any stumbling-block of iniquity for a fellow Jew, or even for a gentile — that one should not give a cup of wine to a nazirite, nor a limb from a living animal to the sons of Noah, nor hand to him what is forbidden to him, nor cause him to stumble in any of the matters that the sons of Noah were warned about.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:82: "You shall not destroy its trees, to wield an axe against them" (Deuteronomy 20:19). We have been warned by this not to cut down any fruit-bearing tree, even to build a siege-work with it, so long as one can find enough barren trees to suffice. And so we have been warned by this not to squander money uselessly, even to the value of a single small coin. And our Sages said: whoever tears his garments to excess over his dead is lashed — and how much more so one who breaks vessels in his anger, for he has done two evils: he has destroyed money, and he has given his anger dominion, transgressing thereby the words of Torah; for from now on he wages war with the inclination of anger, which will lead him to transgress his religion — as it is written (Proverbs 29:22), "and a man of wrath abounds in transgression." And we have already stated for you what our Sages of blessed memory said: if you see a man breaking a vessel in his anger, regard him in your eyes as though he worshipped idols, for such is the way of the evil inclination: today it tells him, Do this, and tomorrow it tells him, Worship other gods. And our Sages of blessed memory said: a man should not pour out the water of his well when others need it. Moreover, we have been warned not to destroy the body by exposing it to danger, or by afflicting the body to consume it needlessly through fasts out of grief and anger, and not to mourn excessively over one's dead. But of one who laments and mourns over his own iniquities it is said (Isaiah 57:18), "I have seen his ways, and I will heal him; I will lead him also, and restore comforts to him and to his mourners." And it is said (Genesis 9:5), "And surely your blood of your lives will I require" — and our Sages of blessed memory said: I will require your blood immediately from your own souls.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:83: "Three years shall it be as forbidden fruit unto you, it shall not be eaten" (Leviticus 19:23). The prohibition of orlah (fruit of the first three years) applies also outside the Land, and it is forbidden even for benefit. And whatever is forbidden for benefit is forbidden to give as a gift to a gentile. Therefore Scripture needed to permit giving carrion to a gentile, to make known that it is permitted for benefit, as it is said (Deuteronomy 14:21), "You shall not eat any carcass; you may give it to the stranger who is within your gates, that he may eat it." And one who gives orlah, or chametz on Passover, or meat cooked in milk to a gentile is lashed; likewise if he places any of these before a dog he is responsible to feed. And the commandments concerning orlah and mixed planting in a vineyard, whether within the Land or outside it, require that these be burned in fire. And if a gentile owns a tree of orlah, it is forbidden for a Jew to gather fruit from it for the gentile's benefit even without payment, since he thereby derives a benefit — the gentile's gratitude toward him. And likewise it is forbidden for a Jew to give a gentile to drink of the gentile's own wine, whether for payment or without payment. And a fourth-year vineyard is forbidden for benefit without redemption, and it may not be redeemed until its fruits reach the season of tithing. And when is the season of tithing? From when their fruits are fully formed, as our Sages of blessed memory taught: from when are fruits liable for tithe.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:84: "Therefore the children of Israel do not eat the sinew of the thigh vein" (Genesis 32:33). The sciatic sinew is forbidden for benefit, and it is forbidden to give it to one's Canaanite bondman or bondwoman. And it is forbidden to send a thigh to a gentile with the sciatic sinew still in it. (And thus the Rosh brings, at the beginning of the chapter Gid Ha-nasheh, in the discussion of one who sends a thigh to a Canaanite, in the name of our author — though the halachah is not decided in accordance with him on this point, but rather like Maimonides and the other decisors, that the sciatic sinew is permitted for benefit, and one may send a thigh to a gentile with the sinew still within it, as is explained in the Tur and Shulchan Aruch, Yoreh Deah, siman 65.)
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:85: "You shall not steal, nor deal falsely, nor lie" (Leviticus 19:11). Our Sages said: "You shall not steal" — even with intent to vex, meaning that a man should not say, I will steal such-and-such a vessel so that its owner will be distressed and disgusted, and become careful in guarding his belongings, and afterward I will return it to him. And it is likewise forbidden to take a vessel from a fellow's house by way of theft, to use it and return it. And one should not steal back his own property from a thief, lest he appear to be a thief himself.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:86: "You shall not practice divination, nor observe times" (Leviticus 19:26). "You shall not practice divination" refers, for example, to those who take omens from a weasel and from birds, or if his bread fell from his mouth, or a gazelle crossed his path, and he says, This is a sign that my way will not succeed, and turns back from his way because of it, and the like — that one should not go seeking omens, whether to perform an act or to refrain from an act because of them. "Nor observe times" refers to fixing times and hours, saying, Such-and-such a day is good to begin a task, such-and-such an hour is difficult to set out; one should not listen to the astrologers of the heavens, but let your heart trust in the Lord, the God of heaven and the God of earth. Therefore it is written concerning this matter (Deuteronomy 18:13), "You shall be wholehearted with the Lord your God." From this we learn that those who observe times and practice divination lack trust, and these corrupt practices are the deeds of the land of Canaan, as it is said (Deuteronomy 18:14), "For these nations which you shall dispossess listen to those who observe times and to diviners, but as for you, the Lord your God has not permitted you to do so."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:87: "You shall do no unrighteousness in judgment" (Leviticus 19:15). Behold, it says afterward, "You shall not favor the poor, nor honor the great; in righteousness shall you judge your neighbor." What then is the "judgment" spoken of at the beginning of the verse? Our Sages of blessed memory said: this refers to measure, weight, and volume, teaching that one who measures is called a judge, and that if he falsified the measure, he is like one who corrupts justice, and is called unrighteous, detestable, banned, and an abomination, and causes five things, like one who perverts justice: he defiles the land, he desecrates the Name, he removes the Divine Presence, he causes the people to fall by the sword, and he exiles them from their land. "In measure" — this is measure of the land; "in weight" — as its plain meaning; "and in volume" — this is the measure of liquid and dry goods. "Just stones" are the weights against which one weighs; an ephah is the measure for dry goods; a hin is the measure for liquid. "I am the Lord your God, who brought you out, etc." — I distinguished in Egypt between the drop that would become a firstborn and the drop that would not, and I am faithful to exact retribution from one who hides his weights in salt, in order to deceive people who cannot detect them.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:88: "You shall not be to him as a creditor" (Exodus 22:24). We have been warned by this not to distress the borrower; the lender should not pass before him when he knows the borrower has nothing to repay, thereby pressuring him and weakening his spirit; and our Sages of blessed memory said that it is as though he judged him with two judgments, as it is said (Psalms 66:12), "You have caused men to ride over our heads; we went through fire and through water." And it is fitting to gird oneself with zeal to rebuke those who trample upon our people in some places by imprisoning the borrower in chains, even when it simply did not happen to be within his means to repay.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:89: "You shall not lay interest upon him" (Exodus 22:24). This is a warning to the witnesses as well, for the lender, the borrower, and the witnesses all transgress a negative commandment. Therefore it says "you shall not lay," in the plural, after having said, "you shall not be to him as a creditor" — since this second is a warning directed to the witnesses.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:90: "There shall be no blemish in it" (Leviticus 22:21). We have been warned by this not to inflict a blemish upon a firstborn animal, even in the present time [when there is no Temple].
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:91: "You shall not plow with an ox and a donkey together" (Deuteronomy 22:10). We have been warned by this not to plow and not to thresh with two different species when they are yoked together by a yoke or a rope; and the same law applies to driving them when yoked together. And its mentioning "plowing" speaks of the common case; even driving them merely by voice, when yoked together, is forbidden. And two mules, one the offspring of a mare and the other of a female donkey, are two different species, and it is forbidden to drive them together; and it is forbidden to drive a mule together with a horse or with a donkey. (Leviticus 19:19), "You shall not let your cattle mate with a diverse kind." A female mule that is in heat may not be mounted by either a horse or a donkey, but only by a male mule of her own kind — meaning, where the mule and the female mule have mothers of the same kind, both being the offspring of a mare or of a female donkey.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:92: "Nor shall you place a figured stone in your land" (Leviticus 26:1). We have been warned by this not to prostrate ourselves upon a stone pavement in a synagogue or in any place other than the Holy Temple.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:93: "Do not make your souls detestable" (Leviticus 11:43). We have been warned by this not to eat things repugnant to the soul — that one should not eat a fish or a locust until it has died; and likewise one should not drink from a cup used by bloodletters. And one who withholds relieving himself transgresses the prohibition of "do not make your souls detestable."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:94: "Do not profane your daughter, to make her a harlot, lest the land fall to harlotry and the land become full of depravity" (Leviticus 19:29). Our Sages explained that this verse comes to warn that a man should not hand over his unmarried daughter for intercourse not for the sake of marriage; "lest the land fall to harlotry" — for if you do so, the land will play the harlot and produce its fruits elsewhere, not in your own land. And so it says (Jeremiah 3:3), "Therefore the showers have been withheld, and there has been no latter rain; yet you have the forehead of a harlot woman." And concubines were permitted without a marriage document and without formal betrothal only to the king, since his dread rests upon people and others would not dare consort with her; therefore the king's exclusive relation to his concubine is akin to marriage. And after the permission granted for concubines to a king, our Sages decreed concerning a bride without a blessing that she is forbidden to her husband like a menstruant.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:95: And behold, you have seen the punishment of one who sets aside an unmarried woman for harlotry, for it is said concerning this, "lest the land fall to harlotry and the land become full of depravity." And one who has relations with an unmarried woman even a single time, by chance, is given lashes of rebellion by the words of the Sages — apart from the great and evil stumbling-block that awaits those who come to an unmarried woman: for she is ashamed to immerse from the impurity of her menstruation in a river or a mikveh, lest the report of her harlotry become known to the public; therefore her impurity remains in her skirts; she gave no thought to her latter end. Our Sages further said (Sanhedrin 76a): "Do not profane your daughter, to make her a harlot" — this is a warning that a man should not marry off his daughter to an old man.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:96: "You shall not eat any carcass" (Deuteronomy 14:21). Our Sages of blessed memory said: whatever becomes invalid through its slaughter is deemed carrion. And it would be pleasant for those who rebuke to testify among the people and to be careful concerning the laws of ritual slaughter and their fine details, to fulfill their requirements completely, and to choose for themselves, in all their statutes, a slaughterer who fears sin — for a great multitude of Israel depend upon him through the commandment of slaughter and inspection. Yet our Sages of blessed memory also said, truthfully, that most of those found engaged in ritual slaughter are experts; still, there are places where, unknowingly and with no one to rebuke, many people are found engaged in slaughter without being expert in the requisite skill. And moreover, we have seen in some of them a scandal: that many of the experts have distanced their hearts from the fear of sin, and one who is not God-fearing, his heart will not comprehend the need to be scrupulous in examining the knife, for one must direct his heart with the utmost concentration in examining it. Do you not see that a man may examine a knife two or three times and not feel a fine notch, and afterward find it — because he finally directed his heart properly, for the sense of touch's discernment follows the direction of the heart? Besides this, a man may act presumptuously without fear in examining the [ritual] signs and the other ways and aspects of the law, as will become evident before all who know the law and its judgments.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:97: "And you shall take no bribe" (Exodus 23:8) — even with the intent to acquit the innocent and condemn the guilty. And even if the two litigants agreed to pay him a fee jointly, our Sages of blessed memory said thus: one who accepts payment to judge — his judgments are void. But they are permitted to pay him the wage for the loss he sustains from being kept from his own work, if the loss is clear, fixed, and known to people, provided that neither of them pays more than the other for the wage of that loss.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:98: Our Sages of blessed memory said: "and you shall take no bribe" — even a bribe of words. For if one of the litigants speaks flattering words to him, he must withdraw his soul from that case. And if the litigant brought him a gift when coming to be judged before him, he should not take it from his hand; and if he had already accepted a gift from him beforehand, and took his gift, this judge has already become disqualified from judging him.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:99: "No manner of work shall be done on them, except what every person must eat" (Exodus 12:16). Our Sages said: since carrying out was permitted for the need of eating on a festival, it was also permitted when not strictly for the need of eating, provided it is for the need of the day — as they said, one may carry out a Torah scroll into the public domain on a festival to read from it on that day; but it is forbidden to carry out for a weekday need, except for the need of the festival. And many of the people sin by carrying out the key to their chest into the public domain on a festival, even when the chest contains none of the food to be eaten on the festival.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:100: "A man shall not wear a woman's garment" (Deuteronomy 22:5). This is a warning against a man removing the hair of his armpit or his pubic area [in a feminine manner].
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:101: "You shall not bring blood upon your house" (Deuteronomy 22:8). This is a warning against keeping a vicious dog or an unstable ladder within one's house.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:102: "You shall not work with the firstborn of your ox, nor shear the firstborn of your flock" (Deuteronomy 15:19). The law of the firstborn applies both within the Land and outside it; and a firstborn animal that becomes mixed among a hundred or a thousand renders all of them forbidden for benefit.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:103: "You shall not do so to the Lord your God" (Deuteronomy 12:4). This is a warning against erasing the Name.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:104: "And you shall not walk in their statutes" (Leviticus 18:3). We have been warned by this to distance ourselves from all the ways of the Amorite, among them charms and amulets that are not from an expert source recognized for healing.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:105: "And you shall eat no bread, nor parched grain, nor fresh grain, until this very day" (Leviticus 23:14). New grain is forbidden by the Torah even outside the Land.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:106: We have written some of the things in which many err unknowingly, since their ears were never opened to them, and some of the things which they know to be forbidden yet do not know the severity of the prohibition; and we have mentioned them so that the erring people not persist in them. Let the wise man hear and add further instruction, to warn the people concerning the things that will befall them because of these; and let the intelligent be reminded, and let them warn as brightly as the shining of the firmament.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:107: The Sixth Level – Death at the Hand of Heaven: the difference between death and excision is that liability for death falls upon him alone and not upon his offspring, while in the punishment of excision, both he and his offspring are cut off. Yet our Sages of blessed memory said that in one respect and from one angle, the severity of death at the hand of Heaven exceeds that of excision: for one who is liable to death at the hand of Heaven will have death rise up through his windows, and the living creatures of his possessions and property die — his cow, grazing on the ashes, dies; his hen, foraging on the dungheap, dies; and death clings to him until it destroys him entirely.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:108: (Perhaps siman 108 is missing, or an error has occurred in the numbering of the sections.)
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:109: And those liable to death at the hand of Heaven are enumerated in part in the Mishnah, such as one who eats untithed produce (tevel) — grain from which terumah and tithes have not yet been separated as required; and this commandment applies in the Land of Israel. And likewise an impure priest who ate pure terumah, and a non-priest (zar) who ate terumah.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:110: And there are among them those which our Sages of blessed memory explained in the Talmud and in the Midrashim, and most of them can be learned from Scripture — such as one who afflicts a widow or orphan, as it is said (Exodus 22:21-23[24]), "You shall not afflict any widow or orphan child. If you afflict him at all, etc., then My wrath shall grow hot." And our Sages of blessed memory said: it is the same whether he cries out or does not cry out — meaning that one who afflicts a widow or orphan is punished regardless, whether the one afflicted under his hand cries out or remains silent; but they hasten to exact retribution from him when the orphan cries out to the Blessed Name.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:111: One who robs the poor, as it is said (Proverbs 22:22-23), "Rob not the poor, because he is poor, etc., for the Lord will plead their cause, and spoil the soul of those who spoil them." We have already explained this at the Third Level. And our Sages of blessed memory said (Bava Kamma 119a) that one who robs the poor is as though he took his very soul from him, as it is said (Proverbs 1:19), "So are the ways of every one that is greedy for gain; it takes away the life of its possessors." Sometimes he damages his livelihood even by robbing him of less than the value of a small coin; therefore blood is reckoned to that man — he has shed blood if he robbed him of even the value of a small coin.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:112: And one who brings forth an evil name (slander), as it is said (Numbers 14:37), "And the men who brought forth an evil report of the land died by the plague before the Lord." Our Sages of blessed memory said (Arachin 15a): if one who brings forth an evil name upon the Land is punished with death, how much more so one who brings forth an evil name upon a man of Israel, who is obligated in Torah and mitzvot. And it is said (Deuteronomy 22:19), "and they shall fine him a hundred pieces of silver, and give it to the father of the young woman, because he has brought forth an evil name, etc." Behold, Scripture did not mention his sin regarding his having sought the woman's life and caused her to be put to death by the court through the false witnesses he brought against her regarding her chastity, but rather mentioned the iniquity of bringing forth an evil name — for this is the greater iniquity, more than one who seeks to end a life, since the pain of humiliation is more bitter than death. And so our Sages of blessed memory said (Ketubot 46a) that for bringing forth an evil name, Scripture obligated lashes and a monetary fine — not for the matter of seeking her death. And our Sages of blessed memory said (Jerusalem Talmud, Bava Kamma 8:7) that one who brings forth an evil name with words that defame a family has no atonement forever, for it does not suffice him to seek forgiveness merely from the living, who are still alive, since he has also caused shame and stench to fall upon their lineage, for those yet to be born of them. And we shall add further explanation of this in explaining the severity of the iniquity of the four factions.
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:113: And one who toys sexually with children, and one who commits adultery whether by hand or by foot, is liable. And our Sages of blessed memory said (Niddah 13b) that his punishment is like the punishment of the generation of the Flood, who corrupted their way. And likewise one who does as Er and Onan did, threshing within and winnowing without, to destroy the seed, is liable, as it is said (Genesis 38:10), "And the thing which he did was evil in the eyes of the Lord, and He slew him also." And it is said concerning those who emit seed in vain (Isaiah 57:5), "inflaming yourselves among the terebinths, under every green tree, slaying the children, etc."
Sha'arei Teshuvah 3:114: And a Torah scholar who does not conduct himself with modesty is liable, since he distances the love of creatures from the Torah. And our Sages of blessed memory said (Shabbat 114a) that of him it is said (Proverbs 8:36), "all who hate me love death" — its meaning: "those who hate me" is to be read as "those who cause me to be hated," for they cause people to hate the Torah. And our Sages of blessed memory said (Yoma 86a): when a man reads Scripture and studies Mishnah, and his speech is gentle with people, and his dealings in the marketplace are pleasant, and he conducts his business faithfully, what do people say of him? Fortunate is so-and-so who studied Torah, fortunate are his father and mother who taught him Torah; woe to people who have not studied Torah — so-and-so who studied Torah, see how pleasant are his ways, how proper are his deeds; of him Scripture says (Isaiah 49:3), "And He said to me, You are My servant, Israel, in whom I will be glorified." But when a man reads Scripture and studies Mishnah, and his speech is not gentle with people, and his dealings in the marketplace are not pleasant, and he does not conduct his business faithfully, what do people say of him? Woe to so-and-so who studied Torah, woe to his teacher and his father who taught him Torah; fortunate are people who have not studied Torah — so-and-so who studied Torah, see how corrupt are his deeds, how ruined are his ways; of him Scripture says (Ezekiel 36:20), "and they profaned My holy name, when it was said of them, These are the people of the Lord, and yet they have gone forth from His land."
